claims.source_title: Time Series Momentum
claims.author_if_known: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
claims.instrument: 58 liquid futures/forwards across equity indices, currencies, commodities (incl. gold) and government bonds
claims.original_claim_summary: Across 58 futures/forward instruments spanning multiple asset classes, the sign and magnitude of a market's own trailing 12-month excess return positively predicts its excess return over the subsequent month, and this pattern is present for nearly every instrument tested individually.
claims.claimed_mechanism: trend persistence: a sustained directional move over roughly a year tends to continue into the near-term future (own-asset time-series momentum)
claims.context: holds across asset classes and time periods 1965-2009 in the original sample; effect is strongest following large absolute past moves
claims.prerequisite_state: a measurable 12-month trailing excess return (positive or negative) in the instrument
claims.event_sequence: 12-month directional trend established -> holding period begins -> return over next 1-12 months continues in same direction as the trailing trend
claims.trigger: sign of trailing 12-month excess return crossing zero
claims.invalidation: trailing 12-month return near zero (no established trend) or after ~12-36 months when the trend historically begins to partially reverse
claims.claimed_outcome: positive expected return when trading in the direction of the trailing 12-month sign, pooled across instruments and time
claims.falsification_condition: If the sign of trailing 12-month excess return showed no statistically significant relationship to next-month excess return out of sample across the instrument panel, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Time Series Momentum
claims.author_if_known: Tobias J. Moskowitz, Yao Hua Ooi, Lasse Heje Pedersen
claims.instrument: 58 liquid futures/forwards across equity indices, currencies, commodities (incl. gold) and government bonds
claims.original_claim_summary: The time-series momentum effect documented over 1-12 month horizons partially reverses over the subsequent 12-24 months, a pattern the authors interpret as consistent with initial underreaction followed by delayed overreaction and correction.
claims.claimed_mechanism: momentum decay and partial mean-reversion at longer horizons following an initial trend-following phase
claims.context: measured in the pooled diversified time-series momentum portfolio across the 58-instrument panel
claims.prerequisite_state: a completed 1-12 month momentum phase already in place
claims.event_sequence: trend continuation for ~12 months -> deceleration -> partial reversal of cumulative gains over months 13-36
claims.trigger: elapsed time since trend initiation exceeding roughly one year
claims.invalidation: no reversal observed in the 13-36 month window following the trend
claims.claimed_outcome: part of the earlier trend-following profit is given back over the following one to two years
claims.falsification_condition: If cumulative time-series momentum returns kept compounding without reversal (or reversed immediately rather than after ~12+ months) in out-of-sample data, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: An Investigation of Transactions Data for NYSE Stocks
claims.author_if_known: Robert A. Wood, Thomas H. McInish, J. Keith Ord
claims.original_claim_summary: Average intraday stock returns follow a U-shape across the trading session: significantly positive returns cluster in the first 30 minutes after the open and again near the close, with lower average returns in the middle of the day.
claims.claimed_mechanism: time-of-day conditioning of realized returns tied to the open and close of the session
claims.context: regular NYSE trading hours, aggregate/cross-sectional average across listed common stocks
claims.event_sequence: market open -> elevated average returns in first 30 minutes -> quieter midday drift -> elevated average returns into the close
claims.trigger: proximity to session open or session close
claims.invalidation: flat or randomly distributed intraday average-return profile with no elevation at open/close
claims.claimed_outcome: higher average realized return concentrated at the open and close relative to midday
claims.falsification_condition: If average intraday returns were flat or higher at midday than at the open/close across a broad equity sample, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: An Investigation of Transactions Data for NYSE Stocks
claims.author_if_known: Robert A. Wood, Thomas H. McInish, J. Keith Ord
claims.original_claim_summary: First-order serial autocorrelation of intraday returns also traces a crude U-shape across the trading day, differing systematically between the open, midday, and close, indicating the return-generating process itself changes with time of day rather than being stationary.
claims.claimed_mechanism: time-varying microstructure/autocorrelation regime across the trading session (non-stationary intraday return process)
claims.context: regular NYSE session, transaction-level data aggregated into intervals
claims.event_sequence: session progresses from open to close -> autocorrelation structure of returns shifts systematically with time-of-day
claims.trigger: time elapsed since open / time remaining to close
claims.invalidation: constant, time-invariant autocorrelation across the session
claims.claimed_outcome: the statistical character of price changes (not just their level) depends on time of day
claims.falsification_condition: If return autocorrelation were statistically indistinguishable across open, midday and close periods, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects
claims.original_claim_summary: Expected stock illiquidity (measured as average daily absolute return per dollar of volume) is positively related to expected stock returns over time, i.e. periods and stocks with higher illiquidity command a higher return premium.
claims.claimed_mechanism: illiquidity risk premium: compensation demanded by investors for the price impact of trading in less liquid conditions
claims.context: cross-section and time series of NYSE stocks; effect more pronounced in small-cap names
claims.prerequisite_state: elevated Amihud illiquidity ratio (absolute return / dollar volume) relative to history
claims.event_sequence: illiquidity rises -> required/expected return rises -> asset repriced downward until higher forward return is consistent with the higher illiquidity
claims.trigger: increase in the illiquidity ratio
claims.invalidation: no relationship between illiquidity level and subsequent realized/expected returns
claims.claimed_outcome: higher expected returns priced into less liquid stocks and time periods
claims.falsification_condition: If stocks/periods with higher measured illiquidity did not show higher subsequent expected returns after controlling for other risk factors, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Illiquidity and Stock Returns: Cross-Section and Time-Series Effects
claims.original_claim_summary: Unexpected (contemporaneous) increases in market illiquidity are associated with negative contemporaneous stock returns and coincide with periods of elevated volatility, i.e. liquidity evaporation and volatility spikes tend to occur together.
claims.claimed_mechanism: liquidity-volatility feedback: a liquidity shock depresses prices in real time and coincides with heightened volatility
claims.context: periods of market-wide stress where liquidity dries up
claims.prerequisite_state: a shock that reduces trading liquidity
claims.event_sequence: liquidity shock hits -> dollar volume falls / price impact rises -> contemporaneous negative return and higher realized volatility
claims.trigger: unexpected rise in the illiquidity ratio relative to its expected level
claims.invalidation: illiquidity shocks with no associated contemporaneous price decline or volatility increase
claims.claimed_outcome: negative contemporaneous return and elevated volatility concurrent with the liquidity shock
claims.falsification_condition: If unexpected illiquidity increases showed no correlation with contemporaneous negative returns or volatility spikes, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy For The U.S. Equity Market
claims.author_if_known: Carlo Zarattini, Andrea Barbon, Andrew Aziz
claims.instrument: Leveraged US equity ETFs (e.g. TQQQ), 5-minute opening range
claims.original_claim_summary: A systematic opening-range breakout strategy that enters in the direction of the first 5-minute candle's break, uses an ATR-derived stop, and exits at market close, produced statistically significant net-of-cost alpha versus buy-and-hold over a multi-year sample.
claims.claimed_mechanism: opening-range breakout continuation: the direction established by the first few minutes of trading tends to continue for the remainder of the session often enough to be exploitable after volatility-scaled risk control
claims.context: high-volatility leveraged ETFs; day-trading horizon with a hard same-day exit
claims.prerequisite_state: price breaks above/below the high/low of the opening 5-minute range
claims.event_sequence: opening 5-minute range forms -> price breaks the range high or low -> position taken in breakout direction -> held to close or ATR-based stop
claims.trigger: close of a 5-minute bar beyond the opening range high/low
claims.invalidation: price reverts back inside the opening range and hits the ATR-based stop before the close
claims.claimed_outcome: positive risk-adjusted return net of realistic transaction costs and slippage over the sample period
claims.falsification_condition: If the same 5-minute ORB rule applied out-of-sample to a new period produced no statistically significant edge net of realistic costs, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Can Day Trading Really Be Profitable? Evidence of Sustainable Long-Term Profits from Opening Range Breakout (ORB) Day Trading Strategy vs. Benchmark in the US Stock Market
claims.original_claim_summary: Opening-range breakout profitability is concentrated in stocks showing abnormally elevated relative trading volume/news catalysts ("stocks in play"); restricting the ORB signal to this subset materially improves results versus applying it to the broad, unfiltered stock universe.
claims.claimed_mechanism: breakout continuation is conditional on elevated participation/liquidity and information flow, not a universal property of any range break
claims.context: requires a volume/news filter to isolate stocks with abnormal same-day activity before applying the breakout rule
claims.prerequisite_state: stock is flagged as having relative volume or news catalyst well above its own historical baseline
claims.event_sequence: screen for abnormal relative volume/news -> opening range forms -> breakout of the range -> continuation more reliable than in an unfiltered universe
claims.trigger: range breakout occurring specifically within the pre-filtered high-activity subset
claims.invalidation: breakout occurring in a stock without abnormal volume/news showing materially worse continuation odds
claims.claimed_outcome: higher win rate / return per trade for filtered vs. unfiltered ORB signals
claims.falsification_condition: If ORB win rate/return were statistically indistinguishable between the volume-filtered subset and the broad unfiltered universe, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Market Intraday Momentum
claims.author_if_known: Lei Gao, Yufeng Han, Sophia Zhengzi Li, Guofu Zhou
claims.original_claim_summary: The market's return in the first 30 minutes of trading (since the prior close) positively and significantly predicts the return in the last 30 minutes of the same trading day, with a scaled slope of about 6.94 and R-squared near 1.6%.
claims.claimed_mechanism: intraday momentum: early-session directional information is only partially impounded and continues to push price in the same direction into the close
claims.context: regular US equity trading session; effect measured on a highly liquid, broad index ETF
claims.prerequisite_state: a measurable first-30-minute return since the prior close
claims.event_sequence: first 30 minutes of session establish a directional return -> midday -> last 30 minutes tend to continue in the same direction
claims.trigger: sign and magnitude of the opening 30-minute return
claims.invalidation: no statistically significant relationship between opening and closing half-hour returns
claims.claimed_outcome: positive, statistically significant predictive relationship between first and last half-hour returns
claims.falsification_condition: If the first-half-hour return showed no statistically significant predictive slope on the last-half-hour return out of sample, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Market Intraday Momentum
claims.author_if_known: Lei Gao, Yufeng Han, Sophia Zhengzi Li, Guofu Zhou
claims.instrument: S&P 500 ETF (SPY) plus 10 other liquid domestic/international ETFs
claims.original_claim_summary: The intraday momentum effect (first half-hour predicting last half-hour) is stronger on days with higher realized volatility, higher trading volume, during economic recessions, and on days with major macroeconomic news releases.
claims.claimed_mechanism: regime-conditioned intraday momentum: predictability of late-session direction from early-session direction increases with informational/volatility intensity of the day
claims.context: high-volatility, high-volume, recessionary, or macro-news days show stronger effect than average/quiet days
claims.prerequisite_state: day is classified as high volatility, high volume, recession, or macro-announcement day
claims.event_sequence: day begins with elevated volatility/volume or scheduled macro news -> first half-hour return recorded -> predictive relationship to last half-hour strengthens versus an average day
claims.trigger: day-level classification as high-activity (volatility/volume/news/recession)
claims.invalidation: predictive slope not meaningfully different between high-activity and quiet days
claims.claimed_outcome: amplified predictability of the last half-hour return conditional on elevated day-level activity
claims.falsification_condition: If the intraday momentum slope were flat (not stronger) on high-volatility/high-volume/news days relative to quiet days, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
claims.instrument: US equity indices (and major international equity indices)
claims.original_claim_summary: US equity indices earned large, statistically significant average excess returns in the 24 hours preceding scheduled FOMC announcements from 1994-2011, accounting for a disproportionate share of total annual equity returns; no comparable effect was found in Treasuries or around other major macro news releases.
claims.claimed_mechanism: pre-scheduled-event drift: prices drift upward ahead of a known, dated monetary policy announcement independent of its content
claims.context: scheduled FOMC meeting days, 1994-2011 sample; effect specific to equities, not Treasuries or money-market futures
claims.prerequisite_state: an FOMC meeting scheduled within the next 24 hours
claims.event_sequence: FOMC meeting date approaches -> equity index drifts upward in the preceding 24-hour window -> drift resolves around/after the announcement
claims.trigger: entering the 24-hour window before a scheduled FOMC announcement
claims.invalidation: no measurable excess drift in equities during the pre-FOMC window relative to comparable non-FOMC 24-hour windows
claims.claimed_outcome: positive average excess equity return concentrated specifically in the pre-announcement window
claims.falsification_condition: If the average equity return in the 24 hours before FOMC announcements were statistically indistinguishable from random 24-hour windows, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Stock Returns over the FOMC Cycle
claims.author_if_known: Anna Cieslak, Adair Morse, Annette Vissing-Jorgensen
claims.timeframe: bi-weekly, keyed to FOMC meeting cycle
claims.original_claim_summary: The entire US equity risk premium is earned in even-numbered weeks (0, 2, 4, 6) of FOMC cycle time, i.e. weeks starting from the most recent FOMC meeting, with odd weeks showing statistically insignificant average excess returns.
claims.claimed_mechanism: cyclical liquidity/policy-communication pattern tied to the roughly six-week FOMC meeting cadence, not a specific announcement-day effect
claims.context: measured relative to elapsed weeks since the last scheduled FOMC meeting, across the full sample period studied
claims.prerequisite_state: elapsed time since last FOMC meeting is an even number of weeks (0, 2, 4, or 6)
claims.event_sequence: FOMC meeting occurs -> weeks 0/2/4/6 from that meeting show concentrated equity risk premium -> intervening odd weeks show flat average returns
claims.trigger: calendar alignment with an even FOMC-cycle week
claims.invalidation: equity premium spread evenly across all FOMC-cycle weeks rather than concentrated in even weeks
claims.claimed_outcome: statistically significant positive average return in even FOMC-cycle weeks; near-zero average return in odd weeks
claims.falsification_condition: If average returns in odd FOMC-cycle weeks were statistically indistinguishable from (or larger than) even-week returns in an updated sample, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Stock Market Prices Do Not Follow Random Walks: Evidence from a Simple Specification Test
claims.author_if_known: Andrew W. Lo, A. Craig MacKinlay
claims.instrument: NYSE/AMEX weekly index and individual stock returns
claims.original_claim_summary: Variance ratios for weekly US equity index and portfolio returns are significantly greater than one at 2- and 4-week horizons, rejecting the random walk hypothesis in favor of positive short-horizon serial correlation; the authors attribute much of this to nonsynchronous trading and small-cap stocks rather than a simple exploitable pattern.
claims.claimed_mechanism: short-horizon positive autocorrelation in aggregated equity portfolio returns, driven substantially by microstructure effects (nonsynchronous trading) rather than pure behavioral momentum
claims.context: weekly return horizons for diversified equity portfolios, particularly small-cap-heavy indices
claims.event_sequence: weekly returns are computed and their variance ratio measured against multiples of the base holding period -> ratio found significantly above 1 at 2-4 week horizons
claims.trigger: computation of the variance ratio statistic at short (2-4 week) aggregation horizons
claims.invalidation: variance ratio statistically indistinguishable from 1 at these horizons
claims.claimed_outcome: rejection of the random walk null hypothesis; evidence of positive short-horizon serial correlation, with a caveat about non-trading-driven artifacts
claims.falsification_condition: If the variance ratio at 2-4 week horizons were not statistically different from 1 in a given sample, the random-walk-rejection claim for that sample would be false.

claims.source_title: Empirical Properties of Asset Returns: Stylized Facts and Statistical Issues
claims.original_claim_summary: Large price changes tend to be followed by further large price changes of either sign, producing slowly-decaying (long-memory) autocorrelation in absolute and squared returns, even though raw signed returns show negligible linear autocorrelation.
claims.claimed_mechanism: volatility clustering: the magnitude of price changes is persistent even though their sign is close to unpredictable at short lags
claims.context: documented across essentially all liquid markets, instruments, and time periods studied in the surveyed literature
claims.prerequisite_state: a recent period of elevated absolute/squared returns
claims.event_sequence: a large-magnitude price move occurs -> probability of subsequent large-magnitude moves (either direction) remains elevated for an extended period -> autocorrelation of |return| decays slowly over many lags
claims.trigger: an above-average absolute return observation
claims.invalidation: autocorrelation of absolute/squared returns decaying immediately to zero (i.i.d. magnitude process)
claims.claimed_outcome: persistently elevated realized volatility following large moves, independent of the direction of the next move
claims.falsification_condition: If the autocorrelation function of absolute/squared returns dropped to statistical insignificance within one or two lags across markets, the volatility-clustering claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Empirical Properties of Asset Returns: Stylized Facts and Statistical Issues
claims.original_claim_summary: Asset return distributions are heavy-tailed (excess kurtosis relative to Gaussian) and exhibit a leverage-type asymmetry where downside volatility tends to be more pronounced than upside volatility of comparable magnitude.
claims.claimed_mechanism: fat tails plus negative return-volatility correlation: large drawdowns coincide with sharper volatility increases than comparably sized rallies
claims.context: documented broadly across equity and other asset return series; the asymmetry is more pronounced in equities than in some other asset classes
claims.prerequisite_state: a negative return of meaningful magnitude
claims.event_sequence: a negative price shock occurs -> subsequent realized volatility rises by more than it would after a comparable positive shock
claims.trigger: occurrence of a large negative return
claims.invalidation: symmetric volatility response to positive versus negative shocks of equal magnitude
claims.claimed_outcome: asymmetric volatility expansion following down-moves relative to up-moves of the same size
claims.falsification_condition: If volatility responded symmetrically to positive and negative shocks of equal size across a broad asset sample, the leverage-asymmetry claim would be false.

claims.source_title: A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns
claims.author_if_known: Dong Lou, Christopher Polk, Spyros Skouras
claims.timeframe: daily, split into close-to-open (overnight) and open-to-close (intraday) segments
claims.original_claim_summary: Cross-sectional stock momentum returns are earned almost entirely during the overnight (close-to-open) session rather than the intraday (open-to-close) session, indicating the momentum premium is concentrated outside of continuous trading hours.
claims.claimed_mechanism: session-specific return concentration: the same signal (past return ranking) produces returns that are segregated by trading session rather than spread evenly through the day
claims.context: cross-sectional momentum-sorted portfolios of US equities
claims.prerequisite_state: a stock's momentum rank (winner/loser) based on trailing past returns
claims.event_sequence: portfolio formed on trailing momentum -> overnight session captures nearly all of the momentum premium -> intraday session contributes little to no momentum premium
claims.trigger: holding a momentum-sorted long-short portfolio through the close-to-open window specifically
claims.invalidation: momentum premium distributed evenly (or concentrated intraday) rather than overnight
claims.claimed_outcome: overnight segment accounts for effectively all of the realized momentum strategy return
claims.falsification_condition: If the intraday session contributed a comparable or larger share of total momentum-portfolio returns than the overnight session, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns
claims.author_if_known: Dong Lou, Christopher Polk, Spyros Skouras
claims.timeframe: daily, split into overnight and intraday segments
claims.original_claim_summary: For several well-known return anomalies (value, profitability, investment, market beta, idiosyncratic volatility, equity issuance, discretionary accruals, share turnover) that earn a statistically significant premium intraday, an economically and statistically significant premium of the opposite sign appears overnight, largely offsetting the intraday effect.
claims.claimed_mechanism: session-level sign reversal: whichever anomaly premium is earned during continuous trading tends to be counteracted by an opposite-sign premium overnight for the same signal
claims.context: cross-section of US equities sorted on multiple established characteristics
claims.prerequisite_state: a stock characteristic sort that produces a significant intraday anomaly premium
claims.event_sequence: characteristic-sorted portfolio earns a premium intraday -> the same portfolio held overnight earns an offsetting premium of opposite sign
claims.trigger: holding the same characteristic-sorted long-short portfolio across both sessions separately
claims.invalidation: overnight and intraday premia for the same characteristic showing the same sign or no relationship
claims.claimed_outcome: combined full-day premium is smaller than either session's premium in isolation, due to the opposing-sign offset
claims.falsification_condition: If overnight and intraday premia for these characteristics moved in the same direction rather than opposing directions in an independent sample, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: A Theory of Intraday Patterns: Volume and Price Variability
claims.instrument: NYSE stocks (e.g. Exxon 1981 data used in the original empirical illustration)
claims.original_claim_summary: Trading volume and price volatility both exhibit a U-shaped pattern through the trading day, high near the open and close and comparatively low around midday, theoretically explained by discretionary liquidity traders concentrating their trades around periods when informed traders are also active.
claims.claimed_mechanism: strategic clustering of discretionary liquidity trading around the open and close, which concentrates both volume and volatility in a U-shape
claims.context: continuous double-auction markets with a mix of informed and discretionary liquidity traders
claims.event_sequence: session opens -> concentrated liquidity trading and information-driven trading co-occur -> volume/volatility spike -> midday lull as discretionary traders defer -> volume/volatility rise again into the close
claims.trigger: proximity to session open or close
claims.invalidation: flat, non-U-shaped intraday volume/volatility profile
claims.claimed_outcome: systematically elevated volume and price variability at the open and close relative to midday
claims.falsification_condition: If measured intraday volume and volatility were flat or highest at midday rather than at the open/close, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: The Tactical and Strategic Value of Commodity Futures
claims.author_if_known: Claude B. Erb, Campbell R. Harvey
claims.original_claim_summary: Commodities whose futures curve is in backwardation (nearby contract priced above deferred contracts) have historically earned higher average returns than commodities in contango; a long-the-most-backwardated/short-the-most-contangoed portfolio outperforms a passive long-only commodity index.
claims.claimed_mechanism: term-structure/roll-yield signal: the shape of the futures curve conditions the expected roll return and realized return of a commodity
claims.context: cross-section of individual commodity futures ranked monthly by their term-structure slope
claims.prerequisite_state: a measurable and persistent slope (backwardation or contango) in the futures curve for the commodity
claims.event_sequence: commodities are ranked by curve slope -> long the most backwardated, short the most contangoed -> portfolio rebalanced periodically
claims.trigger: monthly ranking/rebalancing based on the term-structure signal
claims.invalidation: no meaningful average return difference between backwardated and contangoed commodities
claims.claimed_outcome: positive average excess return to the long-backwardation/short-contango portfolio versus a passive benchmark
claims.falsification_condition: If backwardated and contangoed commodities showed statistically indistinguishable average returns out of sample, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: The Tactical and Strategic Value of Commodity Futures
claims.author_if_known: Claude B. Erb, Campbell R. Harvey
claims.original_claim_summary: Combining a trailing 12-month price momentum signal with the term-structure (backwardation/contango) signal produces higher average returns and improved risk-adjusted performance in commodity futures than using either the momentum or term-structure signal alone.
claims.claimed_mechanism: signal complementarity: momentum and term structure capture different, partly independent sources of predictability in commodity futures returns
claims.context: monthly-rebalanced commodity futures portfolios sorted by combined signal
claims.prerequisite_state: both a trailing 12-month return ranking and a term-structure ranking available for each commodity
claims.event_sequence: commodities double-sorted on momentum and term structure -> combined long/short portfolio formed -> rebalanced monthly
claims.trigger: monthly double-sort and rebalance
claims.invalidation: combined signal performing no better than the better of the two single signals
claims.claimed_outcome: higher average return and/or better risk-adjusted return for the combined double-sorted portfolio versus single-signal portfolios
claims.falsification_condition: If the combined momentum+term-structure portfolio did not outperform the better single-signal portfolio out of sample, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Cultural Calendars and the Gold Drift: Are Holidays Moving GLD ETF?
claims.timeframe: daily, windows around dated cultural/religious festivals
claims.original_claim_summary: Gold (via the GLD ETF) shows a statistically detectable positive price drift in the days surrounding major wealth-oriented cultural and religious festivals across Christian, Islamic, Hindu, and East Asian calendars, attributed to anticipatory physical/gift-related demand rather than standard risk-factor exposure.
claims.claimed_mechanism: calendar-anchored demand shock: recurring, dateable cultural events generate anticipatory buying pressure in gold ahead of the event date
claims.context: windows surrounding specific festival dates (e.g. Diwali, Eid al-Adha, Lunar New Year, Christmas) across multiple cultural calendars, aggregated globally
claims.prerequisite_state: an approaching date on one of the studied cultural/religious calendars associated with gift-giving or wealth rituals
claims.event_sequence: festival date approaches on a relevant calendar -> anticipatory demand builds -> GLD exhibits positive drift in the pre-festival window -> drift dissipates after the date passes
claims.trigger: calendar proximity to a designated festival date
claims.invalidation: no measurable abnormal drift in the GLD price window around the festival dates relative to comparable non-festival windows
claims.claimed_outcome: positive abnormal drift in gold prices concentrated in the pre-festival window, described by the authors as persisting after controlling for standard risk factors
claims.claimed_horizon: days to weeks around each festival date
claims.falsification_condition: If GLD showed no statistically significant abnormal drift around the studied festival dates relative to matched control windows, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Cultural Calendars and the Gold Drift: Are Holidays Moving GLD ETF?
claims.timeframe: daily, windows around dated cultural/religious festivals
claims.original_claim_summary: This is a near-duplicate of SRC-acad-021 (same underlying paper, presented as a Quantpedia blog summary rather than the SSRN working paper) -- unlike festival effects previously documented in local equity or currency markets, the gold festival drift is described as pervasive across national borders because gold trades as a globally accessible, low-correlation safe-haven asset.
claims.claimed_mechanism: cross-border demand aggregation: because gold is a single globally-traded asset (unlike locally-listed equities), festival-driven demand from many separate cultural calendars superimposes onto one price series
claims.context: aggregated across multiple simultaneous or near-simultaneous festival calendars worldwide
claims.prerequisite_state: overlapping or clustered festival dates across more than one cultural calendar
claims.event_sequence: multiple culturally-distinct festival demand shocks occur close together on the calendar -> their gold-buying effects aggregate into a larger combined drift than any single festival alone
claims.trigger: calendar clustering of festival dates from different cultural traditions
claims.invalidation: no additional drift observed when multiple festival windows overlap versus a single isolated festival window
claims.claimed_outcome: larger aggregate drift during periods of overlapping global festival demand than during isolated single-festival periods
claims.falsification_condition: If overlapping multi-calendar festival windows showed no larger gold drift than isolated single-festival windows, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Structural Limits of OHLCV-Based Intraday Signals in MNQ Futures: A Systematic Falsification Study
claims.original_claim_summary: A 5-minute opening-range-breakout long signal on MNQ futures failed to clear realistic round-trip transaction costs out of sample: gross edge across tested configurations ranged roughly 0.07-1.50 points per trade versus an assumed 2-point round-trip friction, and the signal did not reach a T-statistic of 2.0 with consistent direction across 2021-2025 walk-forward folds.
claims.claimed_mechanism: breakout-continuation failure: a range breakout at 5-minute resolution does not carry enough directional edge to survive realistic execution costs, contradicting a naive breakout-continuation assumption
claims.context: single-bar, publicly observable OHLCV-derived opening-range-breakout signal tested with pre-registered walk-forward out-of-sample validation on a liquid index futures contract
claims.prerequisite_state: opening range established and price breaking beyond it, exactly as in a standard ORB rule
claims.event_sequence: opening range forms -> breakout triggers long entry -> position held per rule -> realized gross edge measured against fixed per-trade friction across 2021-2025 out-of-sample folds
claims.trigger: breakout of the defined opening range
claims.invalidation: a version of the signal clearing the pre-registered T-stat, trade-count, cost-hurdle, cross-year-consistency and permutation-test bar simultaneously
claims.claimed_outcome: the ORB-long signal, along with 13 other single-bar OHLCV signal families tested, failed to produce a net-of-cost, statistically robust edge; edge only appeared when using regime classification and multi-bar holding structures rather than a raw single-bar trigger
claims.falsification_condition: If the same ORB-long rule on MNQ produced a net-of-cost T-statistic >= 2.0 with consistent sign across 2021-2025 folds and passed the permutation test, this falsification claim itself would be false (i.e. the signal would in fact have edge).

claims.source_title: Structural Limits of OHLCV-Based Intraday Signals in MNQ Futures: A Systematic Falsification Study
claims.original_claim_summary: Across 14 tested single-bar OHLCV signal families (including gap-continuation and range/volatility-based reversal classifiers), none simultaneously satisfied all five pre-registered falsification criteria (T-stat >= 2.0, >=30 trades per fold, positive net-of-friction returns, consistent direction 2023-2025, and permutation p < 0.001); two positive-control signals (RTH confluence and a London-session signal) were included specifically to validate that the testing framework could detect real edge when present.
claims.claimed_mechanism: systematic overstatement of naive single-bar technical signals: apparent edge in simple OHLCV-derived setups is generally an artifact of look-ahead, small samples, or unaccounted friction rather than a robust, persistent phenomenon

claims.trigger: A 1-minute closing price beyond (open + range x buy multiplier) for longs, or beyond (open - range x sell multiplier) for shorts.

claims.source_title: Larry Williams Market Secrets (Part 5): Automating the Volatility Breakout Strategy in MQL5
claims.original_claim_summary: Rather than using a fixed-point breakout distance, entries and stops are scaled to the prior day's actual range, on the claim that this adapts the strategy to the market's current volatility regime instead of over- or under-triggering during quiet or wild periods.
claims.claimed_mechanism: A volatility-scaled (percentage-of-prior-range) threshold automatically widens during high-volatility periods and narrows during low-volatility periods, keeping the breakout trigger's statistical significance roughly constant across changing market conditions, unlike a fixed-point distance which becomes too tight in volatile periods and too loose in quiet ones.
claims.context: Applies across varying volatility regimes for the same instrument over time.
claims.prerequisite_state: Prior day's high-low range is known.
claims.event_sequence: Range measured daily -> breakout/stop distances recomputed each day as a proportion of that day's range -> thresholds shift automatically as volatility expands or contracts.
claims.trigger: N/A (this is a parameterization mechanism rather than a discrete trigger).
claims.invalidation: If realized volatility diverges sharply from the prior day's range intraday (regime shift within the day), the volatility-scaled threshold may be miscalibrated for that session.
claims.claimed_outcome: Volatility-adaptive thresholds are claimed to produce more consistent breakout signal quality across changing market conditions than fixed-point thresholds.
claims.falsification_condition: If a volatility-scaled breakout system does not outperform an otherwise identical fixed-point breakout system across periods of varying realized volatility, the adaptive-threshold claim is false.

claims.source_title: Developing a Volatility Based Breakout System
claims.original_claim_summary: A break of a defined session's high/low is only treated as a genuine breakout if price also clears a separate ATR-based volatility stop set beyond the session boundary; a break of the session level alone, without clearing the volatility stop, is treated as a false breakout to be faded.
claims.claimed_mechanism: A session-range break that lacks sufficient accompanying volatility/momentum (as measured by ATR) is more likely a liquidity probe that will fail and revert, while a break that also clears a wider ATR-based threshold demonstrates enough force to represent a genuine change in market direction.
claims.context: Applied at the boundary of a user-defined intraday trading session window.
claims.prerequisite_state: A session high/low has been tracked for the current active session, and the corresponding ATR-based volatility stop level (session high + ATR x multiplier, or session low - ATR x multiplier) has been computed.
claims.event_sequence: Session window opens -> session high/low tracked -> price crosses the session boundary -> system checks whether price also clears the ATR-based volatility stop beyond that boundary -> if yes, genuine breakout trade taken in the breakout direction; if no, a counter-directional fade trade is taken instead.
claims.trigger: Price crossing the session boundary; direction of the resulting trade (breakout vs. fade) is determined by whether the corresponding ATR-based volatility stop is also cleared.
claims.invalidation: Each breakout/fade signal is only triggered once per session, preventing repeated re-entry on the same session's level; the opposite classification (fade vs. breakout) would apply if the ATR condition is not met.
claims.claimed_outcome: Requiring the ATR-volatility confirmation is claimed to reduce false breakout signals by ensuring trades are entered only when there is sufficient momentum behind the move.
claims.falsification_condition: If session breaks that clear the ATR-volatility stop do not show a materially higher continuation rate than session breaks that do not clear it, the volatility-confirmation mechanism for distinguishing genuine from false breakouts is false.

claims.source_title: Developing a Volatility Based Breakout System
claims.original_claim_summary: When price crosses the session high/low but fails to also clear the ATR-based volatility stop, the system takes a counter-directional 'fade' trade rather than following the break, on the claim that this specific pattern (weak break without volatility confirmation) tends to revert.
claims.claimed_mechanism: A session-boundary break unaccompanied by expanding volatility indicates the move lacks the momentum needed to sustain a new directional trend, so the initial break is more likely a temporary liquidity-driven excursion that reverts back toward the session range.
claims.context: Applied specifically when a session-level break occurs without the accompanying ATR-based volatility threshold being cleared.
claims.prerequisite_state: Price has crossed the session high/low boundary without clearing the corresponding ATR-based volatility stop.
claims.event_sequence: Session boundary crossed -> ATR-volatility stop not cleared -> fade (counter-directional) trade entered -> managed toward its own risk parameters back into the session range.
claims.trigger: Session-boundary cross combined with failure to clear the ATR-based volatility stop.
claims.invalidation: If price subsequently clears the ATR-based volatility stop after the fade trade is entered, the original 'false breakout' classification is contradicted.
claims.claimed_outcome: The fade trade is claimed to profit from the reversion of a break that lacked sufficient volatility/momentum confirmation.
claims.falsification_condition: If fade trades taken on volatility-unconfirmed session breaks do not outperform simply doing nothing (or following the break) on the same signals, the fade-on-weak-break claim is false.

claims.source_title: Meta-Labeling the Classics (Part 3): Filtering and Sizing Bollinger Band Trades
claims.original_claim_summary: A classic Bollinger Band mean-reversion signal (buy when price touches/closes below the lower band, sell when it touches/closes above the upper band) holds in ranging markets but fails systematically -- not randomly -- during trending markets, where band touches instead mark the start of continued moves.
claims.claimed_mechanism: Band-touch signals encode an assumption that price extension beyond a volatility envelope will revert to the mean; this assumption is only valid when the underlying process is range-bound, and when a trend is forming (high ADX with expanding bandwidth) the same band touches instead reflect genuine momentum, so trading them as mean-reversion produces a systematic (regime-driven) cluster of losses rather than random noise.
claims.context: Regime-dependent: holds during low-ADX, range-bound conditions; fails during high-ADX, trend-establishing conditions with expanding bandwidth.
claims.prerequisite_state: Price closes at or beyond one of the Bollinger Bands.
claims.event_sequence: Price closes at/below lower band (or at/above upper band) -> primary model fires a mean-reversion signal (+1 or -1) -> outcome depends on whether the prevailing regime is ranging (reversion tends to occur) or trending (price continues, causing losses).
claims.trigger: Close at or beyond the lower or upper Bollinger Band.
claims.invalidation: Rising bandwidth combined with high ADX at the time of the band touch signals that the ranging assumption no longer holds, invalidating a naive mean-reversion trade on that touch.
claims.claimed_outcome: In ranging regimes, price reverts toward the middle band after a touch; in trending regimes, the same touch signal is claimed to fail in a predictable, regime-driven way rather than randomly.
claims.falsification_condition: If naive band-touch mean-reversion trades taken during independently-classified high-ADX/expanding-bandwidth periods do not lose at a materially higher rate than those taken during low-ADX/contracting-bandwidth periods, the regime-dependent-failure claim is false.

claims.source_title: Meta-Labeling the Classics (Part 3): Filtering and Sizing Bollinger Band Trades
claims.original_claim_summary: A secondary classifier trained on bandwidth-regime and related features can learn to suppress low-quality Bollinger Band touch signals (occurring in trending regimes) while sizing up high-confidence signals, separating the 'which direction' question from the 'whether to trade at all' question.
claims.claimed_mechanism: Because the failure of the mean-reversion signal is systematic and regime-driven rather than random, a model that specifically learns to detect the trending-regime feature signature (notably a bandwidth-regime feature, 'bb_bw_regime') at the time of a band touch can distinguish high-quality reversion opportunities from low-quality trend-continuation traps, and this probability estimate can also be used to scale position size.
claims.context: Applied at the moment a primary Bollinger Band touch signal fires, before a trade is actually placed.
claims.prerequisite_state: A primary mean-reversion signal (band touch) has fired.
claims.event_sequence: Primary signal fires -> secondary (meta-label) classifier evaluates regime features including bandwidth regime -> classifier outputs a probability of the primary signal being correct -> low-confidence signals are suppressed, marginal signals sized down, high-confidence signals sized up.
claims.trigger: Secondary classifier's confidence probability exceeding a threshold at the time of a primary signal.
claims.invalidation: If the bandwidth-regime feature (or the secondary classifier generally) fails to discriminate between eventual winning and losing band-touch signals out of sample, the meta-labeling approach provides no benefit.
claims.claimed_outcome: Filtering and sizing band-touch signals via the secondary classifier is claimed to improve realized performance relative to trading every band touch identically.
claims.falsification_condition: If meta-labeled (filtered and sized) Bollinger Band trades do not show better out-of-sample risk-adjusted performance than an unfiltered baseline that trades every band touch with fixed size, the meta-labeling claim is false.

claims.source_title: Gold Asian Breakout | Buy Trading Robot (Expert Advisor) for MetaTrader 5

claims.source_title: EURUSD London Session Manipulation (AMD)

claims.source_title: Liquidity Sweep
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster explains liquidity sweeps as a byproduct of large traders slicing unfilled orders rather than deliberate 'stop hunting'. Using a hypothetical chart, they describe how a ranging market between two swing points resolves via a brief break above the range high (liquidating short stops) before reversing hard to make a new low.
claims.claimed_mechanism: Retail short positions accumulate during a range with stops resting just above the range high; a large participant needing to complete a still-unfilled buy program pushes price briefly above that high (triggering stop-loss buying plus breakout-chasing longs), then uses that inflow of liquidity to reverse price sharply lower, breaking to a new swing low.
claims.context: Generic ranging market on any FX pair; applies to a range formed between two identifiable swing points.
claims.prerequisite_state: An established range between two swing points (Pin1 low, Pin2 high) with visible retail short positioning and stops clustered just above the range high.
claims.event_sequence: Price ranges between Pin1 and Pin2 -> brief break above the range high (stop-loss/breakout buying) -> large participant liquidity absorption completes -> price reverses and closes below Pin1, making a new low.

claims.invalidation: If price continues higher after the break rather than reversing, the sweep-and-reverse read is invalidated (this would instead be a genuine continuation/liquidity run).
claims.claimed_outcome: A new swing low is made shortly after the brief break above the prior range high.
claims.claimed_horizon: Not specified (implied intraday to multi-day range resolution)
claims.falsification_condition: If ranges with visible retail short clustering above the high break upward and continue trending higher (rather than reversing to a new low) more often than they reverse, the mechanism as described is falsified.

claims.source_title: Trading the Asian Session

claims.source_title: Stop Hunting
claims.original_claim_summary: Responding to a question about hearing 'market talk of stops being taken out' on a broker squawk service, the poster says retail traders can learn to anticipate stop-hunt levels themselves by watching institutional levels and swing highs/lows where resting orders cluster.

claims.claimed_outcome: Runs of obvious stop-cluster levels precede larger directional moves.
claims.falsification_condition: If price runs of obvious swing-high/low or round-number levels are not followed by directional continuation more often than chance (compared to similar-magnitude moves at non-obvious levels), the claim is falsified.

claims.source_title: Gold Trading – An institutional Way

claims.claimed_outcome: A large, fast directional move ('distribution') shortly after specific session-open windows.
claims.falsification_condition: If gold's realized volatility/range expansion in the minutes after these defined session-open windows is not measurably larger than at randomly chosen intraday times following similarly tight consolidations, the claim is falsified.

claims.source_title: Gold Trading – An institutional Way
claims.original_claim_summary: The same poster claims that during the pre-session consolidation, retail stop-losses resting just below recent swing lows (in the example, ahead of the NY open) get triggered, and that this liquidity is used by larger participants to build a position opposite to the direction the stops were protecting.

claims.source_title: Gold Trading – An institutional Way

claims.source_title: ICT Liquidity Sweep and Liquidity Run Strategy-TFlab
claims.original_claim_summary: Post distinguishes a 'liquidity sweep' (a false break beyond equal highs/lows that quickly reverses) from a 'liquidity run' (a break beyond equal highs/lows that continues in the existing trend), claiming the former is a reversal signal and the latter a continuation signal.
claims.claimed_mechanism: When price briefly breaks above/below a level where equal highs/lows sit (an obvious liquidity pool) and then quickly rejects back into the prior range, that is read as a reversal ('sweep'). When price breaks the same kind of level and keeps moving in the direction of the existing trend without rejecting back, that is read as trend continuation ('run').
claims.context: General price action around equal-highs/equal-lows liquidity pools, most emphasized at London/NY session opens.
claims.prerequisite_state: A recognizable equal-highs or equal-lows liquidity pool from recent price action.
claims.event_sequence: Price approaches equal highs/lows -> breaks beyond them -> either (a) quickly rejects back inside the range (sweep -> counter-trend reversal trade) or (b) continues without rejecting (run -> trend-continuation trade).
claims.trigger: A close beyond equal highs/lows; the trigger for direction is whether/how quickly price closes back inside the prior range.
claims.invalidation: For the sweep read: a failure to reject back into range invalidates the reversal read. For the run read: a rejection back into range invalidates the continuation read.
claims.claimed_outcome: Reversal after a sweep; trend continuation after a run — the same visual break can resolve either way depending on whether an established trend is already present.
claims.falsification_condition: If, controlling for prior trend state, breaks of equal highs/lows show no differential rate of reversal vs. continuation, the sweep/run distinction is falsified as merely a post-hoc labeling of outcomes.

claims.source_title: ICT Liquidity Sweep and Liquidity Run Strategy-TFlab

claims.source_title: Gold Trading Strategy – New York Open Range Breakout Scalping
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster defines the New York equity open range on gold using the first ~2 minutes after 9:30am ET (M1 chart) and claims a breakout candle qualifies as a valid continuation signal only if its body exceeds 60% of its total range and its open-close range exceeds 1.6x the 14-period ATR.

claims.context: Gold (XAUUSD), New York cash equity open, 9:30-9:50am ET.
claims.prerequisite_state: A defined opening range from candles between 9:30 and 9:32 ET.

claims.claimed_horizon: Within the NY session (minutes to a few hours)
claims.falsification_condition: If gold breakout candles meeting the stated body-size and ATR-multiple thresholds do not show a higher continuation rate than non-qualifying breakout candles of similar size, the filter's claimed predictive value is falsified.

claims.source_title: Gold Trading Strategy – New York Open Range Breakout Scalping
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster explains why the 9:30-9:32am ET range 'works': institutions cannot fill large orders instantly, so they slice orders via VWAP/TWAP execution during the first minutes of the session, and the resulting tug-of-war between retail market orders and institutional limit orders is what forms the opening range.

Once early positioning is complete, obvious stop clusters beyond the range get triggered, producing the breakout expansion.
claims.context: Gold, first minutes of the New York cash equity session.
claims.prerequisite_state: Active institutional order-slicing (VWAP/TWAP-style execution) occurring in the first minutes of the session.

claims.invalidation: Not directly falsifiable at the level of a single trade; falsifiable only in aggregate (see falsification_condition).

claims.claimed_horizon: First 20 minutes of the NY session
claims.falsification_condition: If opening-range breakouts on gold show no greater post-breakout continuation/volatility than breakouts of similarly-sized ranges formed at other, non-open times of day, the microstructure explanation is falsified as the driver of ORB performance.

claims.source_title: M5 Mean Reversion Strategy
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster describes a counter-trend mean-reversion scalp on gold's 5-minute chart: price closing beyond the outer Bollinger Band while RSI(3) is in an extreme zone (<10 or >90), then closing back inside the band while RSI crosses back through the 10/90 level, is claimed to revert to the middle Bollinger Band about 90% of the time.

claims.context: XAUUSD, M5 timeframe, counter-trend scalping specifically (not trend-following).
claims.prerequisite_state: Price is a 'considerable distance' from the 200 EMA and has closed beyond the outer Bollinger Band with RSI(3) beyond the 10/90 extreme.

claims.claimed_outcome: Reversion to the middle Bollinger Band, claimed to occur roughly 90% of the time within a short window.
claims.falsification_condition: If a transparent backtest of the stated RSI(3)/Bollinger Band rule on XAUUSD M5 does not show reversion to the mid-band occurring anywhere near the claimed ~90% rate, or if the no-stop-loss martingale-style position adding produces large tail-risk drawdowns during trending periods, the claim (as a safe, high-hit-rate edge) is falsified.

claims.source_title: EURUSD Session Breakout and Reverse Strategy
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster claims that on EURUSD M15, when price breaks out of a defined session range (Asian, EU, or a specific afternoon window) and a later candle closes back inside the range beyond the original breakout candle's low/high, price continues moving against the original breakout by roughly the size of the breakout candle or more.

claims.falsification_condition: If an independent, out-of-sample backtest of the failed-breakout-and-reverse rule on EURUSD does not reproduce a positive edge comparable to the poster's reported ~2,200 pips/year, the claim is falsified as an artifact of overfitting to the original one-year dataset.

claims.source_title: 5m TF Price Action Strategy
claims.original_claim_summary: Discussing profit targets, poster states that price rarely 'bursts through' the previous day's high or low, and treats these levels as good places to bank profit or expect a reaction.

claims.context: General intraday FX trading on major pairs, used as a profit-target heuristic within a broader price-action/trend-following approach.
claims.prerequisite_state: An open trade approaching the previous day's high (in an uptrend) or low (in a downtrend).

claims.trigger: Price nearing the previous day's high or low.
claims.invalidation: A session that closes clearly beyond the previous day's high/low without stalling would count against the heuristic for that instance.
claims.claimed_outcome: Price 'rarely bursts through' the prior day's high/low, making it a reasonable profit-target or reaction zone.
claims.falsification_condition: If the measured frequency with which price closes decisively beyond the previous day's high/low is statistically similar to the frequency of stalling/reversing there, the 'rarely bursts through' claim is falsified.

claims.source_title: $* Statistical London Breakout Strategy *$
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster claims that on EURUSD H1, about one hour after the London open, price frequently makes a small, quick break beyond the high or low of the first London hourly candle before reversing and trending strongly the rest of the day in the opposite direction — calling this 'the breakout of the breakout'.

claims.prerequisite_state: A completed first London-session hourly candle with defined high and low.

claims.invalidation: If price does not later move a larger distance in the opposite direction after the small breakout is hit, the 'breakout of the breakout' trend-catching component fails for that day.

claims.claimed_horizon: Rest of the London/NY session (several hours)
claims.falsification_condition: If a systematic test of the two-order breakout structure on EURUSD H1 does not show the second (trend-following) order outperforming a simple immediate-breakout order over a large sample of days, the 'breakout of the breakout' edge is falsified.

claims.source_title: Understanding Order Blocks in Forex Trading
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster explains 'order blocks' in plain terms: the last ranging/consolidation zone immediately before a strong impulsive move that breaks structure is expected to act as support (after a bullish impulse) or resistance (after a bearish impulse) when price returns to it.
claims.claimed_mechanism: Large institutional orders are assumed to be placed gradually within a consolidation range rather than all at once; when an impulsive move breaks away from that range, the range itself is treated as the location of leftover/large institutional orders, so a return visit to that price zone is claimed to trigger a reaction that continues the original impulsive direction.
claims.context: General FX price action; applies to any consolidation range immediately preceding a structure-breaking impulsive move.
claims.prerequisite_state: A ranging/consolidation zone immediately followed by a strong impulsive move that breaks the range structure.
claims.event_sequence: Price consolidates in a range -> an impulsive move breaks out of the range in one direction -> price later retraces back into the high-low zone of the pre-impulse range -> price reacts (holds/reverses) at that zone and resumes the original impulsive direction.
claims.trigger: Price retracing back into the marked pre-impulse consolidation zone.
claims.invalidation: If price trades through the marked zone without reacting and continues in the retracement direction instead, the order-block reaction is invalidated.
claims.claimed_outcome: A reaction (bounce/reversal) at the pre-impulse consolidation zone that resumes the original impulsive move's direction.
claims.falsification_condition: If price revisits of pre-impulse consolidation zones do not show a statistically higher rate of continuation-direction reaction than revisits of arbitrarily chosen equivalent-sized price zones, the order-block reaction claim is falsified.

claims.source_title: Simple easy LOPEN strategy (eurusd)
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster describes marking the Asian-session range (03:00-10:00 broker time) on H1 and claims that when price closes clearly beyond that range between 1-2 hours after the London/NY opens, the move tends to continue in that direction for the rest of the session; if price is still inside the Asian range at that check-time, no trade is taken.

claims.claimed_outcome: Continuation of the breakout direction for the remainder of the session (held until next candle close or 17:00 broker time).
claims.claimed_horizon: Rest of the trading day (several hours)
claims.falsification_condition: If H1 closes beyond the Asian range in the 11:00-17:00 window do not show higher continuation rates through session end than a random sample of similarly-timed candle closes, the continuation claim is falsified. Note: this directly contradicts sweep-and-reverse claims (e.g. SRC-ff-001, SRC-ff-007) about the same type of session-range break, which this research batch deliberately preserves rather than resolves.

claims.source_title: Simple easy LOPEN strategy (eurusd)
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster adds a filter: if the prevailing trend direction on a pair points toward the side with the higher (less favorable) swap/rollover rate, the breakout is more likely to be range-bound or reverse soon rather than continue, and such setups should be avoided.
claims.claimed_mechanism: A trend that requires carrying a costly negative-swap position is treated as a sign of weak conviction/positioning imbalance, making continuation less reliable and a reversal or range condition more likely.
claims.context: Same Asian-range-breakout setup as SRC-ff-013, used as an additional filter before taking the continuation trade.
claims.prerequisite_state: A candidate breakout trade in the direction of the higher negative-swap side for that pair.

claims.trigger: Breakout direction coinciding with the less favorable (more negative) swap side.
claims.invalidation: If breakouts in the costlier-swap direction perform no worse than breakouts in the cheaper-swap direction, this filter provides no value.

claims.falsification_condition: If breakouts aligned with the higher negative-swap direction show similar or better continuation rates than breakouts aligned with the favorable-swap direction, the swap-based filter is falsified.

claims.source_title: Volatility breakout system
claims.original_claim_summary: Poster, discussing prior London/NY-open box-breakout systems, notes that when the final consolidation candle used to draw the opening 'box' closes very close to the box's own upper or lower boundary, the subsequent breakout is more prone to faking out; they propose centering/sizing the box using the hourly ATR around that candle's close instead.
claims.claimed_mechanism: A box breakout system defines a range from a fixed pre-open window; if the last candle before the breakout window closes near the edge of that box, there is very little room left for a genuine expansion move to clear the box significantly, so minor noise is more likely to trigger a breakout signal that then fails (fakeout). Sizing the box relative to the hourly ATR around the candle's close, rather than a fixed pip range, is claimed to reduce this fakeout tendency.
claims.context: London/NY session-open box-breakout systems on FX, using a fixed pre-open time window to draw the box.
claims.prerequisite_state: A pre-session consolidation box whose final candle closes near one of the box's boundaries.
claims.event_sequence: Box is drawn from a fixed time window -> final candle before the session open closes near the box edge -> price breaks the box shortly after -> breakout frequently fails and reverses (fakeout).
claims.trigger: The box-defining candle closing very close to the box's high or low.
claims.invalidation: If breakout success rates are unrelated to how close the defining candle closed to the box edge, the claim is invalidated.
claims.claimed_outcome: Higher fakeout rate for box breakouts when the defining candle closes near the box boundary; proposed fix is ATR-based box sizing centered on the candle's close.
claims.falsification_condition: If box breakouts show no difference in fakeout rate based on how close the defining candle closed to the box boundary, the proposed relationship (and the ATR-centering fix) is falsified.

claims.source_title: London Breakout Strategy Indicator – Most Volatile Session!

claims.prerequisite_state: A visually 'clean' (low-noise) Asian-session consolidation range.
claims.event_sequence: Clean Asian range consolidation forms -> London session opens -> price falsely breaks one side of the range (sweep) -> market structure shift occurs -> displacement move follows in the opposite direction -> price is expected to react at nearby unfilled gaps or prior session highs/lows.

claims.claimed_horizon: Within the London session (a few hours)
claims.falsification_condition: If, following visually 'clean' Asian-range consolidations, the initial break direction at London open continues at least as often as it reverses, the claimed sweep-then-reverse tendency is falsified. Note: this claim, together with SRC-ff-013/014, illustrates the recurring contradiction in these communities between 'session-range breaks reverse' (sweep/SMC framing) and 'session-range breaks continue' (momentum/ORB framing) for what is visually the same event.

claims.source_title: BB Squeeze Breakout — Indicator by Alpha_Wizard
claims.original_claim_summary: Author describes markets moving through a compression phase (Bollinger Bands narrow) followed by an expansion phase where volatility increases and a directional move can start; the indicator flags breakout bars with confirmation filters (RSI, volume, OBV, MACD, bandwidth) after price closes outside the bands for a required number of consecutive bars.

claims.falsification_condition: If measured post-squeeze (post-compression) realized volatility/expansion moves showed no statistically higher continuation or follow-through than random comparable non-squeeze periods, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: BB Squeeze Breakout — Indicator by Alpha_Wizard
claims.original_claim_summary: The script's logic implies not every squeeze release turns into a sustained trend: it separates a 'post-squeeze context' state so a release with weak confirming volume/momentum is treated differently from one with strong confirmation, using signal tiers (BUY vs WEAK BUY) and warning that some breakouts fail.
claims.claimed_mechanism: A breakout out of a volatility squeeze is only reliable when confirmed by concurrent momentum/volume expansion; unconfirmed squeeze releases frequently fail and the market re-enters a compressed/ranging state.

claims.prerequisite_state: Price has already broken out of a Bollinger Band squeeze (an initial release has occurred).

claims.falsification_condition: If breakout follow-through rates (measured forward return / MFE) were statistically indistinguishable between 'confirmed' and 'unconfirmed' squeeze releases, the claim that confirmation predicts follow-through would be false.

claims.source_title: Apollo: VWAP Rejection Indicator by InvestiShare
claims.original_claim_summary: The author frames VWAP as a level institutional traders defend during trend pullbacks; when price touches VWAP, prints a doji (slowdown), and is followed by an engulfing candle with a volume spike in the trend direction, this is read as a continuation signal rather than a reversal.

claims.context: Trending market where price is positioned correctly relative to a 200-period EMA (i.e., a trend filter must agree with the signal direction).
claims.prerequisite_state: Price above (for longs) or below (for shorts) the 200-period EMA, establishing directional bias, prior to the VWAP touch.

claims.invalidation: No engulfing follow-through, or the engulfing candle forms against the prevailing trend direction; price closing decisively through VWAP against the trend.
claims.claimed_outcome: Price resumes the pre-pullback trend direction after the VWAP rejection, rather than reversing.
claims.falsification_condition: If, across many instances of a doji-at-VWAP followed by a trend-direction engulfing candle plus volume spike, the forward continuation rate were no better than a random pullback baseline, the claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Apollo: VWAP Rejection Indicator by InvestiShare
claims.original_claim_summary: The indicator requires simultaneous alignment of a 200-period EMA trend filter with the VWAP-touch/doji/engulfing/volume pattern, implying the VWAP rejection pattern alone is not treated as sufficient and must agree with the higher-timeframe trend bias.
claims.claimed_mechanism: A VWAP touch/rejection signal is more reliable as a trend-continuation trigger when it aligns with a higher-timeframe directional filter (price on the correct side of a 200-period EMA) than when taken in isolation.

claims.prerequisite_state: Price already positioned on the trend side of the 200 EMA before any VWAP touch is considered.
claims.event_sequence: EVENT A: price sits on the trend side of the 200 EMA (bias established) -> transition: VWAP touch + doji + engulfing + volume filter all align with that bias -> EVENT B: the signal is taken; if price is on the wrong side of the 200 EMA, the same VWAP touch pattern is disregarded.
claims.trigger: Simultaneous alignment of EMA-side positioning with the VWAP rejection pattern (all conditions cited in the script).
claims.invalidation: EMA and VWAP-touch signals disagree (price beyond the EMA filter is inconsistent with the VWAP rejection direction).
claims.claimed_outcome: Signals filtered by trend agreement are more trustworthy than VWAP-touch patterns taken without the EMA filter.
claims.falsification_condition: If VWAP-touch continuation signals taken without any EMA trend filter performed no worse (equal win rate/expectancy) than those filtered by the 200 EMA, the added value of the trend filter claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Kaufman Efficiency Ratio Gate [NovaLens] — Indicator by NovaLens
claims.instrument: XAUUSD (gold), author states parameters generalize to other assets
claims.original_claim_summary: The indicator computes Kaufman's Efficiency Ratio (net directional move divided by total path length over N bars) and classifies the market as trend-favorable when the ratio is high versus chop-dominant when it is low, with parameters tuned on gold price data.
claims.claimed_mechanism: The ratio of net directional price change to the sum of absolute bar-to-bar price changes over a lookback window measures what fraction of price movement was 'efficient' (directional) versus noise; values near 1 indicate a trending regime and values near 0 indicate a choppy/range-bound regime.
claims.context: General regime-classification context, tuned by the author using gold (XAUUSD) price data and claimed to generalize to other assets.
claims.prerequisite_state: At least roughly 50-100 bars of price history available to compute a stable ratio.
claims.event_sequence: EVENT A: efficiency ratio computed over N bars -> transition: value compared against a rolling median/threshold -> EVENT B: regime classified as trend-favorable (gate open) or chop-dominant (gate closed).
claims.trigger: Efficiency ratio crossing above/below its rolling median threshold.
claims.invalidation: None explicit; author states the metric is backward-looking and doesn't guarantee the next bar continues the classified regime.
claims.claimed_outcome: Trend-following signals should be more reliable when the gate is open (high ER); mean-reversion or no-trade approaches are more appropriate when the gate is closed (low ER).
claims.falsification_condition: If forward returns/volatility-adjusted performance of trend-following systems showed no improvement when gated by high-ER periods versus low-ER periods (on the same instrument and sample), the regime-utility claim would be false.

claims.source_title: Kaufman Efficiency Ratio Gate [NovaLens] — Indicator by NovaLens
claims.original_claim_summary: The description suggests using the efficiency ratio to switch strategy families: trend-following systems should be favored when the market is efficient/trending (high ER) and mean-reversion systems should be favored when the market is noisy/choppy (low ER).

claims.prerequisite_state: A computed efficiency ratio value for the current lookback window is available before deciding which strategy family to activate.
claims.event_sequence: EVENT A: efficiency ratio computed -> transition: compared to a threshold to classify noise level -> EVENT B: a trend-following module is activated when ER is high; a mean-reversion module is activated when ER is low.
claims.trigger: Efficiency ratio crossing a chosen noise threshold.
claims.invalidation: Regime persists but the selected strategy type underperforms anyway (e.g., a 'trending' market by ER measure that whipsaws due to gaps or news).

claims.source_title: Advanced Market Profile - Automated Volume Profile Indicator by iMetaX

claims.original_claim_summary: The paper tests the plain-language version of the ICT 'liquidity sweep/grab' idea (price temporarily pierces a session extreme, then closes back inside) on 6,442 identified events in MNQ futures, and finds neither fading the sweep direction nor trading with it produces a statistically positive net return after realistic transaction costs (both T-statistics strongly negative, around -13 to -14).
claims.claimed_mechanism: Price piercing a session high/low and closing back inside it (a liquidity sweep) does not, on its own, predict either a reversal (fading the sweep) or a continuation (trading with the sweep) on 5-minute bars once realistic round-trip friction is applied; the gross directional content around such sweeps (0.20-0.80 points) is smaller than the cost of executing the trade.
claims.context: MNQ intraday index futures, Asia-session extreme sweeps identified systematically over 2022-2025 under walk-forward out-of-sample testing.
claims.prerequisite_state: Price has pierced a session extreme (high or low) and closed back inside the prior range, forming an identified liquidity-sweep event
claims.event_sequence: EVENT A: price pierces a session extreme -> EVENT B: price closes back inside the range (sweep confirmed) -> tested outcome: neither fading nor following this event produces a statistically positive net return after costs.
claims.trigger: Confirmed liquidity-sweep event (pierce + close back inside)
claims.invalidation: A version of this test with a positive, cost-adjusted, out-of-sample T-statistic above 2.0 in either direction
claims.claimed_outcome: No tradable directional edge exists purely from the sweep-and-close-back-inside pattern at 5-minute bar-close execution once transaction costs are applied
claims.falsification_condition: This claim (a negative/null finding) would itself be falsified if a comparable walk-forward, cost-adjusted test of the same sweep-and-close-back-inside pattern on MNQ or a similar liquid futures instrument produced a statistically significant positive net return (T >= 2.0) in a consistent direction across multiple out-of-sample years.

claims.original_claim_summary: An Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-style intraday mean-reversion signal was tested directly on Micro Gold Futures (MGC) 5-minute bars across multiple z-score thresholds and both long/short directions; every configuration produced a negative net return after instrument-appropriate transaction costs across 2023-2025.
claims.claimed_mechanism: A statistical model assumes gold's intraday price reverts toward a rolling mean once it deviates by a given number of standard deviations (an OU/mean-reversion process); entering against the deviation (fading extended moves) at several threshold levels, on 5-minute MGC bars, produces a negative average return per trade once realistic round-trip costs (0.50 points) are subtracted, in every tested configuration and year.
claims.context: Micro Gold Futures (MGC), 5-minute intraday data, 2023-2025 (2025 partial), threshold-based mean-reversion entries.
claims.prerequisite_state: Price has deviated from its rolling mean by more than the tested z-score threshold (1.5 or 2.0)
claims.event_sequence: EVENT A: MGC 5-minute price deviates beyond the threshold from its rolling mean -> EVENT B: a mean-reversion trade is entered against the deviation -> tested outcome: average net return after costs is negative across all thresholds, directions, and years tested.
claims.trigger: Price crossing the specified z-score deviation threshold from its rolling mean
claims.invalidation: A version of the test with a positive net-of-cost average return for at least one threshold/direction combination, consistent across years
claims.claimed_outcome: Intraday mean-reversion fading of extended gold-futures moves is not profitable after realistic costs at any of the tested thresholds
claims.falsification_condition: This negative finding would be falsified if a comparable walk-forward, cost-adjusted OU mean-reversion test on MGC (or closely related gold futures) 5-minute data produced a statistically positive, cost-adjusted net return in a consistent direction across multiple out-of-sample years.
